legend: Riana got really bored one day and decided to play with some integers. She started with the positive integer %%ZSMJ0%%. She then noticed that %%ZSMJ1%% was too small and boring. Suddenly, she got the idea to create a really big integer. To do so, she multiplied all of the positive divisors of %%ZSMJ2%% and got the integer %%ZSMJ3%%. After getting the value of %%ZSMJ4%%, she challenged her friend Cisco to determine the value of the original integer %%ZSMJ5%% given %%ZSMJ6%%. Help Cisco find the value of %%ZSMJ7%%.
input: The input contains one line containing the integer %%ZSMJ8%%. It is guaranteed that %%ZSMJ9%% is a positive integer less than %%ZSMJ10%%.
output: Output the original integer %%ZSMJ11%% if possible. Otherwise, output %%ZSMJ12%%.
note: In the first test case, the positive divisors of 4 are 1, 2, and 4. The product is 8.
In the second test case, there is no integer whose product of its positive divisors is 4.
